description: Calculated decoherence timescales in the brain, about 1e-13 to 1e-20 seconds, are far shorter than the relevant dynamical timescales of about 1e-3 to 1e-1 seconds, for neuron firing and for kink-like excitations in microtubules alike.

sources.quote: We find that the decoherence timescales (∼ 10−13 − 10−20 seconds) are typically much shorter than the relevant dynamical timescales (∼ 10−3 − 10−1 seconds)
